chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Muhammad Al-Qasany, from Suleiman ibn Dawood, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

In the will of Luqman to his son: O my son! Travel with your sword, your slippers, your turban, your tent, your water container, your needle, your threads, and your awl. Take provision with you of medicines that benefit you and those with you. And be in concordance with your companions, except in the disobedience of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
ai.seo_question: What did Luqman advise his son regarding travel and companionship?
ai.summary: This narration from Luqman al-Hakim to his son, preserved in al-Kafi, underscores the Shia emphasis on balancing spiritual devotion with worldly pragmatism during travel. It instructs the traveler to carry both physical necessities like weapons and medical supplies, and social tools for maintaining harmony with companions, provided this sociability does not compromise obedience to God. This reflects the broader Islamic principle of 'tawassu' fi al-umur' (expansion in affairs) while remaining anchored in taqwa.
